title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & response formatting
author: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer (/v1/chat.completions) to parity with expected parameters and behavior used by downstream clients. This PR implements: 1) complete mapping for OpenAI-style params (temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, max_tokens, n, logprobs), 2) canonical role handling (user/system/assistant) and robust fallbacks for missing/null roles, 3) stop token handling including multi-token stops and early termination semantics, 4) logprobs support in non-streaming and streaming paths (best-effort for GPU-backed runtime), 5) improved streaming stability and backpressure handling for function/tool call streams, and 6) response formatting adjustments to match OpenAI edge-cases (trailing newlines, role-only deltas, empty content buckets). The description below contains a short checklist and implementation notes. Checklist: - [x] Parameter mapping and validation layer - [x] Role canonicalization and tests - [x] Stop token semantics + unit tests - [x] Logprobs plumbing + integration tests - [x] Streaming stability fixes (chunk boundary handling, flush semantics) - [x] Function/tool call streaming compatibility - [x] SDK compatibility adjustments (python/ts) - [x] Docs and release notes. Implementation notes: The compatibility layer now normalizes incoming chat messages to Redwood's internal message model earlier in the request path to simplify branching. Stop tokens are applied in the runtime token filter and again at the streaming boundary to ensure deterministic early termination in both sync and streaming clients. Logprobs are computed when a downstream model/kernel supports token-prob output; for models without explicit logprob kernels we return nulls per OpenAI contract and surface a warning metric. Streaming changes add a small buffered window to maintain token boundary integrity and reduce partial JSON chunks when function/tool call objects are emitted. This avoids flaky parsers on the SDK side. Backwards compatibility: existing Redwood routes remain unchanged; the OpenAI compat layer is opt-in behind the /openai/* endpoints. Related: ENG-4821 (compat parity epic), ENG-4850 (streaming stability).
commits: feat(openai-compat): add param mapping for top_p, frequency/presence penalties, max_tokens and n
fix(runtime): ensure canonical role normalization for null/unknown roles
feat(streaming): buffered streaming window to prevent partial JSON tool/function messages
feat(logprobs): plumb logprob outputs through inference runtime (best-effort)
test: add unit/integration tests for stop tokens, roles, streaming boundaries
docs: update openai compat docs and examples for chat.completions parity
review_comments: Liam: Can you add a unit test for multi-byte stop tokens? Observed a corner-case in the tokenizer where emojis break early-termination.
Maya: Added test_tokenizer_multibyte in test_stop_tokens.py and verified behavior across utf-8 inputs.
Priya: Streaming: we still saw partial JSON when a function call object spanned two chunks. Can we ensure we never flush mid-object?
Maya: Updated stream_manager to buffer until complete JSON object boundaries for tool/function call events and included a stress test that simulates chunk splits.
Carlos: logprobs implementation looks good, but we should return nulls for unsupported models instead of raising. Add a metric so we can monitor fallbacks.
Maya: Switched to nulls for unsupported kernels and added openai_compat_logprobs_fallback counter.
notes: Observability: added metrics for compat fallbacks and streaming chunk reassembly failures. These are useful for future tuning if customers report parsing issues. For logprobs we surface best-effort values and explicitly document model limitations in the docs. SDKs updated to coalesce streaming delta events into role/content diffs to mirror OpenAI client behavior.
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: parameters (temperature, top_p, penalties, max_tokens, n), role normalization, stop tokens, logprobs (best-effort), improved streaming stability and function/tool call streaming. Backwards compatible and opt-in via /openai/* endpoints.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash. CI green. No follow-up migrations required; monitoring dashboards added to track streaming reassembly and logprobs fallbacks.
